evidence: Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ for '_ckpt' round-trip costs, 'conditional PUT' per-namespace-per-epoch, and 'catalog GET per fold round'. The catalog-GET-per-fold-round part is corroborated (CasRefLedger.cpp:354 'never born costs one catalog GET and stops there'; CasGc.cpp:3724 'One catalog GET replaces the pool-wide LIST'), and _ckpt as a point-GET control object is real (CasFormat.cpp:146). But the compound quantitative estimate ('about two serial S3 round trips per committed chunk', 'one conditional PUT per touched namespace per epoch transition') is a synthesized cost analysis not stated verbatim anywhere in code or comments; cannot confirm the specific counts.

Confirmed 'defer_decision' is a real GC phase (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:640 GcPhaseTimer t(phase_sink, "defer_decision") and changed_shards metric at CasGc.cpp:652), consistent with the claim's mechanism (full LIST run regardless of changed_shards). Grepped the whole repo for the exact figures '177000'/'177,000', '5096.39'/'5,096.39', and '79.11' — no hits outside unrelated files (jeprof heap dumps, unrelated worktree files). The specific T15 soak measurement numbers are not present anywhere in the repository.

Both docs/superpowers/models/CaGcAckFloorCore_empty_blobs.cfg and docs/superpowers/models/CaGcAckFloorZombie_empty_blobs.cfg exist at HEAD with CONSTANTS Blobs = {} and all Sabotage* flags FALSE (i.e. an unperturbed run), checking INVARIANTS TypeOK/INV_NO_DANGLE/INV_NO_RETURN(/INV_ACK_LE_VIEW for Core). No 'CaGcAckFloorCore_empty_blobs_TTrace_*' or 'CaGcAckFloorZombie_empty_blobs_TTrace_*' counterexample trace files exist in docs/superpowers/models/, consistent with these configs having passed without a violation.

No 'CaGcLeaseCore_empty_actors_TTrace_*' counterexample file exists in docs/superpowers/models/, consistent with this config passing green.

Confirmed 'generation retention' is a real GC mechanism at HEAD (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.h:848 'Attempt-scoped generation retention. The sole reclaimer -- bounded per round and fail-open...') and 'gc/' prefix bookkeeping classification is real (utils/ca-soak/scenarios/framework/assertions.py:158). Searched utils/ca-soak/ and the whole repo for '2822', '3.7 MiB', 'B174' as a code tag, and 'generation retention' measurement text — found no trace of the specific 12h-soak measurement (82%, 2822 retained generations, 8:1 ratio); this is a historical soak-run result not recorded in the repository.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.h:61 states directly: 'blob in-degree is a pool-wide property and no ownership partition of the blob space exists', confirming blobs are pool-wide. Refs are namespace-scoped via src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Primitives/CasNamespaceLifeId.h (NamespaceLifeId keyed per table/replica incarnation), i.e. per-replica manifests. Together these confirm a blob's in-degree aggregates edges across every replica's manifest naming it.

Searched the whole repository for 'ASan.*battery', 'LOGICAL_ERROR-abort classification', 'Class A'/'Class B' groupings, and the figure '910' / '~700/910' — no hits except unrelated content (a gdb stacktrace log with coincidental numeric matches). This is a claim about a specific external investigation/battery run's findings that leaves no artifact in the tree; cannot verify or refute from the codebase.

The generation-bump-plus-backward-floor pattern for format migrations is real: src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Formats/CasFormat.h:30 ('kContiguousRefStreamsGeneration as a backward floor. Pools below the floor must be recreated') and :42 ('kNamespaceLifeKeyedGeneration is the backward floor for this change'). Quiesced recreation exists as CasRefLedger::quiesceRefTablesForRemount (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.cpp:1685), invoked from CasPool.cpp:1179 before a remount claims. This matches the claim's description of the required generation-migration pattern (bump generation+floor, quiesce before reuse).

The `no-content-addressed-storage` tag is real and used across many stateless tests (e.g. tmp/cpp-cleanup-worktree/tests/queries/0_stateless/02980_s3_plain_DROP_TABLE_ReplicatedMergeTree.sh, utils/cas-carve/carve.sh:412), so the tag-sync concern names a real artifact. But the claim is about a migration design document's risk-register content ('the design's Scope §4', 'the Claude skills that reference it') which is a planning statement, not something derivable purely from code; found no risk-register or migration-plan artifact in the searchable (non-.md-under-docs/superpowers) tree to confirm the specific risk enumeration.

Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ for 'codecs v3', 'codecs_v3', 'CasCodecsV3' — no matches (the codecs-v3 migration is complete and left no such literal marker in code). This claim is a sequencing/gating statement about when a refactor is allowed to start relative to an 8-step migration; that is a planning constraint, not a code fact, and no artifact enumerating '8 migration steps' as a gate condition was found.

Searched for 'rebirth', 'verbatim-file rebirth aliasing', 'manifest-less orphan', 'condemn-nothing REBUILD' in src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/. Rebirth-aliasing concerns are extensively addressed in current code (e.g. src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Primitives/CasNamespaceLifeId.h:96 'the rebirth alias this type exists to close'; CasRefCatalogFormat.h:65 'makes rebirth structurally inert instead of an alias'), suggesting these were later closed as design invariants, but this is a claim about a past Stage A snapshot-in-time's residual list (with issue ids R1/R4) rather than a current-HEAD fact, and no artifact tying R1/R4 to Stage A specifically was found in code.

HEAD's fetch-by-relink confirm protocol is version 11, not 12: src/Storages/MergeTree/DataPartsExchange.cpp:108 'constexpr auto REPLICATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION_WITH_CA_CONFIRM = 11;' (with REPLICATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION_WITH_CA_RELINK = 10 at line 103). The behavioral shape the claim describes (older/mixed versions degrade to bytes rather than an unconfirmed relink) is correct and implemented at DataPartsExchange.cpp:400-401 ('mixed versions degrade to bytes, never to an unconfirmed relink'), but the version number is 11 at HEAD, contradicting the claim's 'protocol version 12'.

This is a claim about a migration plan's task sequencing ('Task 16', 'coverage matrix', 'user approves') — a project-management artifact, not a code fact. Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ and docs/en for any gating mechanism or task-numbering reference; found none, as expected for a planning-process claim with no code counterpart.

Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Formats/CasRefSnapshotFormat.h/.cpp and CasRefLogFormat.h/.cpp for 'deterministic', 'key-derived identity', and rename/copy-on-create semantics. Found only unrelated 'deterministic' usages (test-clock determinism, e.g. CasRefLedger.h:286/298/377). No text confirms or denies that snapshot/log object bodies repeat key-derived identity fields or that a snapshot is never renamed/copied on creation; could not locate a discriminating fact either way.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefProtocol.cpp:718-735, function `admits`: previews an op on a scratch RefTableState copy and returns false if `encodedSnapshotBudgetSize(scratch) > snapshot_budget` (line 733) or if `encodedRemovalBudgetSize(scratch) > removal_budget` (line 735) — admitting only when BOTH the encoded snapshot and encoded namespace-removal transaction stay within budget, checked on a scratch/preview copy before any durable object is created.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.cpp:1383-1414: the recovery attempt loop restarts (fresh attempt, re-derives its base) when 'a selected snapshot kept vanishing between the checkpoint that named it and its GET' (line 1403-1404), bounded by kRefRecoveryMaxRestarts before giving up; absence is treated as a retryable race, not corruption, and no fallback to an older snapshot is coded — each restart re-derives from a fresh read.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Backend/CasBackend.h:125: 'keys contains only the requested prefix and the cursor resumes strictly after the last returned key; an empty cursor marks the end of the enumeration' (struct ListPage, next_cursor field, line 129: 'Last returned key; empty => no more pages').

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:1728-1753: 'A malformed ref-object key or namespace aborts ref folding for the whole round: the round produces no ref delta, advances no cursor, and authorizes no destructive work -- recorded as an anomaly ... never a throw that wedges the round.' The catch block sets ref_folding_aborted=true and records an anomaly rather than adopting a partial ref_tables map.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasOrphanManifestSweep.cpp:575-586: 'Exact-token delete: HEAD for the current token, then deleteExact' — cleanup deletes only the exact key+token it just enumerated, never a prefix wildcard. src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:1686 confirms the fold 'walks by exact key from the cursor'. Namespace identity is keyed by an opaque per-life NamespaceLifePhysicalId (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Primitives/CasNamespaceLifeId.h), so a recreated namespace gets fresh incarnation-scoped keys distinct from the removed incarnation's exact keys.

Checked docs/superpowers/models/CaRetiredInRun.tla, the add-only-model source most relevant to blob meta lifecycle (Condemned/Clean states appear in src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:107,114 as C++ policy comments, confirmed by prior evidence). CaRetiredInRun.tla's only round action is 'FoldRound ==' (line 192); no 'FoldAbort' action name exists in this file, and no companion TLA source in docs/superpowers/models/ defines a 'FoldAbort' action either. src/Disks/tests/gtest_cas_ref_statemachine.cpp:793-794: 'Randomized replay equation: replay(snapshotOf(mid-state), tail) == full replay (spec §Table State).' TEST(CASRefStateMachine, ReplayEquationPropertyTest) exercises exactly the recovery invariant the claim describes (replaying from a snapshot plus surviving later log entries equals full-history replay), matching prior evidence's RefTableState equation at src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefProtocol.h:187.

docs/superpowers/models/CaErasureProof.tla models exactly this invariant: its cfg variants (_nogc_grace 'writers only, grace ON -> MUST HOLD', _sab_nograce 'writers only, grace OFF -> VIOLATES (zombie lands after promotion => grace IS load-bearing)', comments at lines 63-70) prove that cleanup erasure must not remove an object a still-completing writer/reader needs, gated by a grace period. This is the TLA-verified correctness property matching the claim; docs/superpowers/models/CaErasureProof.tla is a model source file, not corpus prose.

Confirmed the real function is named `admits` (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefProtocol.cpp:718), not 'admit()', and the real ProfileEvent is `CASRefQueueWaitMicroseconds` (src/Common/ProfileEvents.cpp:774), not 'CasRefQueueWaitMicroseconds'. `admits` copies the whole RefTableState per call (CasRefProtocol.cpp:726 'RefTableState scratch = state;') but no comment or test documents its complexity as O(NlogN), and grepping the whole repo for '454 ms' / '454ms' found no matches. Cannot confirm the specific complexity classification or the historical average-latency figure.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefProtocol.h:158: 'uint64_t snapshot_log_count_threshold = 256;' confirms the current default matches the claim's post-change value (256). src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.cpp:3976 uses `publishable_count > config.snapshot_log_count_threshold` as the trigger, and CasRefLedger.cpp:313 (resolveRef) plus RefTableRuntime (CasRefLedger.h:74) implement the copy-once-from-live publication pattern the claim describes (publishable-count accounting rather than a separate tail_since_snapshot counter, consistent with prior evidence).
